question: How is the structure of health infrastructure and health care system in India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Three-tier system**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The health infrastructure and health care system in India is organized in a **three-tier system**.
 
• This system comprises the **primary, secondary, and tertiary** levels of care.
 
• **Primary level** includes sub-centers and primary health centers (PHCs) which are the first point of contact for the community.
 
• **Secondary level** includes community health centers (CHCs) and district hospitals that provide more specialized care.
 
• **Tertiary level** includes medical colleges and specialized hospitals which offer advanced medical services and treatments.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• India's health care system is governed by both the central and state governments, with public and private sectors playing significant roles.
 
• The central government is responsible for formulating national health policies and providing technical and financial support to the states.
 
• State governments are primarily responsible for the delivery of health services and implementation of health programs.
 
• The National Health Mission (NHM) aims to strengthen the health system, particularly in rural and underserved areas.
 
• India's health care system faces challenges such as resource constraints, unequal access to services, and the need for improved infrastructure and workforce.
